rv.q: Slanted Floors is both a plea for, and a fascinating example of, creativity and human connection unmediated by the tyranny of the screen.
To be clear, “Slanted Floors” is a deeply impressive production in many ways.
The slice of life play doesn’t add up to all that much, serving mainly as a tiny portrait of the lives of two characters who we don’t get to know all that well.
Billy McEntee’s intimate two-hander Slanted Floors finds high stakes in the smallest domestic rituals, and Kyle Beltran and Adam Chanler-Berat play them with unnerving, lived-in precision.

cn.t: Critics find *Slanted Floors* a mostly compelling exercise in intimacy, with strong performances from Chanler-Berat and Beltran in a one-bedroom apartment setting. Reception is mixed-to-positive, praising its voyeuristic concept while noting uneven execution.

vr.q: it is certainly a very unique experience with or without soup
